text: {"frames":["'Mind the nets!' shouted Sjoerd Knoopgat from the canal wall. The fishing nets have tangled into one great knot across the lock gate, and the boats cannot pass until someone finds the way through. The plan of the Tower's water routes shows the way in three parts: {a}, {b} and {c|cell|cells|cells}. Each cell on the plan stands for {d} m of real canal. How many metres long is the route?","The brass map of the dyke paths has vanished from its hook beside the tulip gate. Old Wiebe Millsail searches the windowsill, the clog basket and the cheese shelf, but it is nowhere to be found. Only a torn copy of the plan is left, and it shows the dyke walk in three parts: {a}, {b} and {c|cell|cells|cells}. Each cell on the plan stands for {d} m of real dyke. How many metres long is the dyke walk?","You push open the greenhouse door, and warm wet air rushes out to meet you. A tall stem with pale blue petals stands in the middle of the tomato bed, and nobody in the Tower remembers planting it. The gardener, Sientje-of-the-Dyke, wants to know how far the path runs from the door to the glass wall. The path is marked on the plan in three parts: {a}, {b} and {c|cell|cells|cells}. Each cell on the plan stands for {d} m of real path. How many metres long is the path?","A creak and a groan roll down the stairs from the barn, and a smell of warm flour and hay drifts after it. The miller, Joost Mallemolen, has run out of room for his sacks, so he is moving them along the route from the barn to the quay. The plan marks the route in three parts: {a}, {b} and {c|cell|cells|cells}. Each cell on the plan stands for {d} m of real ground. How many metres long is the route?","A small silver fish flips past your boot in the middle of the polder, where yesterday there was only grass. The water is rising through the sluice, and the farmer, Trijntje Klomp, needs to know how far the flood will reach along the ditch. The ditch is drawn on the plan in three parts: {a}, {b} and {c|cell|cells|cells}. Each cell on the plan stands for {d} m of real ditch. How many metres long is the ditch?"]}
